messages.author: e14ab5843c32249d
messages.subject: Parallelization of processes on HPC
parts:
Hi all,
Has anyone written a guide to utilizing MSstats in an HPC environment? More specifically how and when to parallelize using the current MSstats package (4.0+)? I've looked around and can't find anything such as a script or Rmd file. I did read the most current paper but couldn't figure out what parts would be most amenable to parallelization.
Thanks so much for any leads!

Cheers
Carlos

messages.author: 5c6e92c10ef28984
messages.subject: Re: Parallelization of processes on HPC
parts:
Hi,
currently there is no such guide. I'll try to prepare one.
Please find a short summary below.
MSstats uses data.table for all tabular operations (which means almost everything). Data.table has some native parallelization which can be set via R options(). 
Some parts of the workflow are less amenable to parallelization than others: it's good to normalize data before using MSstats.
Then, there are two major functions: dataProcess and groupComparison. Both are just wrappers around MSstats 4.0 workflow that uses functions called MSstatsX like MSstatsSummarize.
For dataProcess, operations that lead to protein-level summarization are implemented this way:

    peptides_dict = makePeptidesDictionary(as.data.table(unclass(raw)), normalization)
    input = MSstatsPrepareForDataProcess(raw, logTrans, fix_missing)
    input = MSstatsNormalize(input, normalization, peptides_dict, nameStandards)
    input = MSstatsMergeFractions(input)
    input = MSstatsHandleMissing(input, summaryMethod, MBimpute,
                                 censoredInt, maxQuantileforCensored)
    input = MSstatsSelectFeatures(input, featureSubset, n_top_feature,
                                  min_feature_count)
    processed = getProcessed(input)
    input = MSstatsPrepareForSummarization(input, summaryMethod, MBimpute, censoredInt,
                                           remove_uninformative_feature_outlier)

    input_split = split(input, input$PROTEIN)
    summarized = tryCatch(MSstatsSummarize(input_split, summaryMethod,
                                           MBimpute, censoredInt,
                                           remove50missing, equalFeatureVar),
                          error = function(e) {
                              print(e)
                              NULL
                          })

    output = MSstatsSummarizationOutput(input, summarized, processed,
                                        summaryMethod, MBimpute, censoredInt)
    output

where fractions handling is optional, normalization can be done beforehand, imputation and selection are optional (and one feature selection method is not fully parallelizable).
So the most important step is the summarization. MSstatsSummarization call can be replaced by per-protein parallelized loop that uses the input_split object are MSstatsSummarizeSingleProtein function.

Similarly, groupComparison has this kind of workflow that can be run in parallel for different proteins.
We will be working on adding better HPC support in the nearest future.

Kind regards,
Mateusz Staniak
